classification.difficultyReason: Translate a majority condition into a binomial event and multiply its probability by the number of experiments.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If six dice are rolled one hundred times, how many times would you expect the number of even numbers showing to exceed the number of odd numbers showing? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

answer.worked:
For one set of six dice, let $X\sim B\left(6,\frac12\right)$ record the number of even results. Even results exceed odd results when $X>3$.
$$\begin{align*}P(X>3)&=\frac{\binom64+\binom65+\binom66}{2^6}\\P(X>3)&=\frac{22}{64}\\\text{Expected number}&=100\left(\frac{22}{64}\right)\\\text{Expected number}&=34.375\approx34\text{ times}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If eight coins are tossed sixty times, how many times would you expect the number of heads to exceed the number of tails? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

answer.worked:
For one set of eight coins, let $X\sim B\left(8,\frac12\right)$ record the number of heads. Heads exceed tails when $X>4$.
$$\begin{align*}P(X>4)&=\frac{\binom85+\binom86+\binom87+\binom88}{2^8}\\P(X>4)&=\frac{93}{256}\\\text{Expected number}&=60\left(\frac{93}{256}\right)\\\text{Expected number}&=21.796875\approx22\text{ times}.\end{align*}$$
